subsystem.name: GenericRuntimeObjects
subsystem.responsibility: Game-wide generic runtime helpers reused across loaders, parsers, settings, audio, UI and network paths: linked-list directory enumeration with path building, a flag-dispatched file/stream object, a normalized-key data and audio-channel hash table, string utilities, standalone file utilities, and network session/receive plumbing.

summary: Reconstruction of the generic runtime-object helpers in the packet address range 0x00565E00-0x0057F300. The functions group into: (1) a DirectoryIterator that recursively enumerates files/subdirectories over a linked list of entry nodes, builds paths, and advances a cursor; (2) a FileStreamObject carrying a handle at +0x0, a dispatch flag at +0x10, and a stream parameter at +0xC, whose close/read/write/line operations dispatch on that flag to different backends and which also serves as the line-oriented settings parser; (3) a KeyedDataHashTable that normalizes string keys, hashes them into at most nine buckets, and chains audio-related keys into a separate channel chain, and loads audio files into itself; (4) small StringUtils and FileIoUtilities free-function groups; (5) network plumbing: a NetworkEventMatcher, a mutex-protected NetworkReceiveQueue, a NetworkSession start path, and a MutexProtectedPointer accessor. Two functions (0x00565F70 double-indirect getter, 0x00567740 mask-extract) stay ungrouped because their owner objects are not evidenced. All class boundaries and field names are DERIVED or GUESS proposals on top of packet evidence; raw source and validated IR outrank worker synthesis.

function_roles.role: Path separator search: locate the last backslash in the iterator's current path string and return the position just after it.
Advance the enumeration cursor to the next list node (peek); true while a current node with a non-null data pointer exists.
Position the enumeration cursor at the first node; begin file/directory enumeration.
Double-indirect field getter: dereference this, read and return the DWORD at the object's +0xC. Vtable-style accessor used by vehicle, scene and tire-brand loaders; owner object not evidenced.
Recursive directory/file enumerator: reset and reentrancy-guarded walk of a path, descending into subdirectories when the flag is set, invoking the per-file visitor for each non-directory entry.
Current-path builder: concatenate the entry's base directory and name into the path buffer, optionally normalize against an additional path string; returns the constructed path or 0.
Case-insensitive substring search over a haystack; returns a pointer to the first matching run or 0. Shared name/token matching helper.
Initializer for the 25-byte stream struct (zero DWORDs at 0x0/0x4/0xC/0x10/0x14, -1 sentinel at 0x8, zero byte at 0x18); returns the object pointer.
Cleanup wrapper: delegate to the flag-dispatched handle close, then free the heap object at +0x4 when present; returns the free or close result.

Open an audio stream on the receiver: close the previous handle, prepare a 1024-byte scratch buffer, open the file, store handle and stream parameter, set initialized/active flags, copy the filename when the handle is valid.
Conditional file-handle close: when the close-method flag at +0x10 is zero close the handle directly, else close through the type-checked stream dispatch; null the handle on success.
Backend-dispatch read/write wrapper: forward to the buffered reader when the +0x10 flag is non-zero, otherwise to the thread-safe read wrapper; return the selected backend's result.

Variadic formatted-write dispatcher: direct locked file write when the mode flag at +0x10 is zero, otherwise format into a local buffer and fill the buffer sink, returning true only when every byte is written.
Line-reading dispatch: when the flag at +0x10 is non-zero read through the line-input reader, else read until newline from the raw FILE handle; returns the line buffer.
Dual-path dispatcher on the selector at +0x10: string-length dispatch when non-zero, string-write-to-file otherwise; true when the selected path returns something other than -1.
Mask-extract of a 16-bit stack value with 0x300 (bits 8 and 9); reads an uninitialized local, likely a decompiler artifact of an FPU control-word read by physics/tire callers.

Line-oriented settings parser on a stream object: read lines, trim, recurse on a leading '{', return on '}', split the key at '.', and dispatch each key/value pair to the keyed-data processor with the base directory from +0x4.

Load an audio file into the receiver's hash table: initialize a local stream struct, open the audio stream, register the stream, load file settings/data, close and clean up; returns whether the load succeeded.

Insert a normalized key/value pair into the data hash table: hash the normalized key into bucket 0..8, allocate a 44-byte entry, copy the strings, and chain the entry either into a caller list or into the hash bucket (audio keys into the channel chain).

Name lookup wrapper: forward the receiver and a name string to the hash-table lookup with flag -1 and return its result; legacy ABI label implies an audio-channel stop path but the visible body is only a lookup.
File-attributes existence/cleanup helper: toggle the read-only attribute (flag 128) then delete the file; true when the delete succeeded.
Sanitize a string into an output buffer under a size budget, encoding characters that need escaping as '+~XX' hex escapes and copying recognized '+~XX' runs verbatim.
Weighted file checksum: open the file, seek to 0, read bytes accumulating a sum of byte times a cycling multiplier, close; returns 1 on success.
Accessor that reads the DWORD at this+0x0 and delegates it to a mutex-protected pointer read-release helper; placed in the session/network layer by its callers.
Network event key comparison: dereference the event comparison structure at this+0x1C and test it against a two-component query key using two alternative match patterns; true when either matches.

Receive the next network packet from a mutex-protected list: build a query key, wait on the mutex, walk the list testing each node with the event matcher, write the matched node's field to the output, release the mutex.

Network session start: query the config sub-object through its vtable, fill a config buffer, obtain a connection object through the main vtable, configure socket parameters, dispatch the mode, and run the session.

classes.name: DirectoryIterator
classes.responsibility: Recursive directory/file enumeration: maintains the linked list head pointer, the enumeration cursor, the managed path string, the raw-path/normalize flag and a reentrancy counter; builds and normalizes entry paths.

classes.name: LinkedListNode
classes.responsibility: Node in the enumeration linked list: a data pointer to the directory entry and a next-node pointer; the cursor lives in the head structure, not the node.

classes.name: DirectoryEntryData
classes.responsibility: Per-entry data structure reached from the enumeration node's data pointer; holds the base directory string used when building the full path.

classes.name: FileStreamObject
classes.responsibility: Generic file/stream object reused across camera, scene, text/UI, vehicle, config, audio and damage-model paths: holds a handle at +0x0, a dispatch flag at +0x10 selecting the close/read/write/line backend, a stream parameter at +0xC, and active flags; also parses line-oriented settings into the keyed-data hash table.

fields.name: string_or_heap_ptr
fields.type_guess: void* (string buffer, base directory or heap object)

classes.name: KeyedDataHashTable
classes.responsibility: Settings/audio data hash table keyed by normalized strings: registers loaded streams, hashes keys into up to nine buckets, classifies audio-related keys into a separate channel chain, and looks names up. Loads audio files whose settings/data are parsed into itself.

classes.name: StringUtils
classes.responsibility: Free string-processing helpers: case-insensitive substring search and the sanitize/hex-escape encoder used by settings, path, file-IO and audio-open paths.

classes.name: FileIoUtilities
classes.responsibility: Free file-IO helpers: read-only-attribute toggle plus delete, and the weighted file checksum.

classes.name: NetworkEventMatcher
classes.responsibility: Tests a received network event against a two-component query key using two alternative match patterns inside the event comparison structure at this+0x1C.

classes.name: NetworkReceiveQueue
classes.responsibility: Mutex-protected receive queue: guards a packet linked list (head/cursor/tail) with a mutex and timeout, walks the list matching each node's event key, and writes the matched node's field to the caller output.

classes.name: NetworkSession
classes.responsibility: Network session start/configuration: resolves a config sub-object, queries and fills a config buffer through its vtable, obtains a connection object through the main vtable, configures socket parameters, and dispatches the session mode.

classes.name: MutexProtectedPointer
classes.responsibility: Accessor for a pointer value at this+0x0 whose read is delegated to a mutex-protected read-release helper; used by session/network-layer callers.

transitions.on: character is '+' (43) and StringPrefixPatternCheck recognizes an existing '+~XX' escape at the cursor
character requires encoding per the per-character classification

interfaces.name: StreamBackendDispatch
interfaces.purpose: Selects a file/stream backend from the dispatch flag at +0x10: buffered reader, thread-safe reader, raw FILE line read, locked direct file write, or string-length dispatch. A replacement must reproduce the flag-to-backend selection for close/read/write/line operations.

interfaces.name: DirectoryEntryVisitor
interfaces.purpose: Per-file callback invoked by the recursive enumerator for every non-directory entry found during a file scan.

compatibility_contracts.name: StreamHandleCloseContract
compatibility_contracts.description: A stream/file object stores a handle at offset 0x0 and a close-method flag at offset 0x10. Closing must use the direct locked close when the flag is zero, otherwise the type-checked stream dispatch, and must null the handle after a successful close. A replacement must preserve both close paths and the null-after-close invariant.

compatibility_contracts.name: DirectoryEnumerationCursorContract
compatibility_contracts.description: Directory enumeration advances a cursor at obj+0x8 over nodes whose data pointer sits at node+0x0 and next pointer at node+0x4. A reentrancy counter at obj+0x21C gates reset/pop, and subdirectory recursion increments then decrements it. A replacement enumerator must reproduce cursor advance, the reentrancy gate, and the per-file visitor call.

compatibility_contracts.name: MutexProtectedPacketQueueContract
compatibility_contracts.description: The receive queue guards its packet list (head +0xAC8, cursor +0xAD0, tail +0xAD4) with a mutex at +0xAD8 and timeout at +0xADC. A replacement must acquire/release the mutex around the list walk, match each node's event key, and write the matched node's field at +0x14 into the caller output, returning a match flag.

compatibility_contracts.name: KeyedDataHashTableInsertionContract
compatibility_contracts.description: Settings/audio data entries are keyed by a normalized string hashed to a bucket index 0..8 (keys hashing above 8 are rejected). Entries carry a key string and an optional value string, and audio-related keys chain into a separate channel chain. A replacement loader must reproduce the normalization, the bucket limit, and the audio-channel classification.

unresolved: Owner classes for most functions are UnknownObject in the packet; the class grouping here (DirectoryIterator, FileStreamObject, KeyedDataHashTable, etc.) is a DERIVED/GUESS proposal, not recovered source.
0x00565F70 double-indirect getter: the object type behind this+0x0 and the meaning of the DWORD at obj+0xC are unknown; the function stays ungrouped.
0x00567740 reads an uninitialized stack local and masks it with 0x300; likely a decompiler artifact of an FPU control-word read by physics/tire callers, so it stays ungrouped with semantics LOW.

FileStreamObject +0x4 has three different evidenced roles (audio filename string buffer, settings base directory, freeable heap object); the single shared field is a proposal and may actually be distinct per subsystem.
The two close paths of 0x00566B90 and the read/write/line backend selection keyed on +0x10 are inferred from the dispatch structure, not proven by an independent source.
0x00566CF0 selector interpretation (string-length lookup versus string-write-to-file) is inferred; whether the value at +0x0 is a string, stream handle or internal buffer is undetermined.
Which keys classify as audio via 0x00568210 and what the +12 channel chain represents are not established.

The 44-byte data entry layout (key at dword index 4, value at index 6, chain and back-link fields at indices 3/9/10) and the hash bucket array are not represented as class fields because the packet provides no flat field refs for them.
Directory entry layout beyond the base directory at +0x144 (e.g. entry name at +0x30) is partially inferred and not evidenced by packet field refs.
Globals aS_4 (0x005C2C18), aSS_3 (0x005C2D64) and asc_5C2AB4 (0x005C2AB4) are referenced by the recursive enumerator but the association with inline '%s'/'%s\\%s' format literals is unconfirmed.
Globals byte_FF00000000005396 and byte_FF0000000000539E carry out-of-range addresses and appear to be decompiler artifacts; their role is unknown.
MutexProtectedPointerReadRelease has no callee address in the packet; whether the delegated read acquires a lock (making 0x0057A900 non-side-effect-free) is unconfirmed.
The network session's three indirect vtable callees (+12, +16, +88) are unresolved; the socket parameter tuple (0, 10, 1, 2, -1) meaning is unknown.
The receive-queue query key (family 2, port 0, address 0) as a sockaddr_in bind/match key and the two match patterns of 0x0057B840 (two record layouts versus two variants) are inferred.
The copy destination this+0xA84 in 0x0057E940 has no packet field ref and is evidenced only through the callee and raw source.
Whether 0x00565F20 is a pure peek or also consumes nodes is decided by caller semantics and is not settled by this packet.
